title: Buy three nines
intro: A replica fleet failing and healing in accelerated time. Redundancy is the only thing between you and the pager.
briefing: One fragile node: it fails every ~20 hours and takes 90 minutes to repair. The business demands THREE NINES (99.9%) by design, but each replica costs real money — you get at most 3. Kill a node yourself and watch what redundancy does. Design nines = what your configuration guarantees; observed availability = the life this particular fleet is living.
debrief: One node gives u = MTTR/(MTBF+MTTR) ≈ 7% downtime — barely one nine. Because active-active replicas fail independently, the service is only down when ALL are: unavailability u^n. Two replicas → 99.5%; THREE → 99.97% — past your target without touching the hardware's reliability. You can also buy nines by shrinking MTTR (faster repair), which is often cheaper than more replicas: availability = MTBF/(MTBF+MTTR) rewards recovering fast just as much as failing rarely. Redundancy turns unreliable parts into a reliable system.
